name: Glass atrium (玻璃中庭温室)
notes: Origin: the gallery floor directly below the painting's viewpoint; +Y runs across the gallery towards the far curtain wall, +X along it, Z up; metres.

Gallery: a glass floor (top at z = 0) on polished jade beams over the garden, south of y = 4.18 and on the west wing; the stairwell (x -5.0..-2.16, y -1.6..4.18) and the atrium north of the edge are open.  The edge is guarded by a frameless glass balustrade whose top edge carries short jade stanchions between two rails (0.91 and 1.04 m) -- the painting draws the stanchions only between the rails.

Through the atrium the view falls on the paved north end of the garden (1 m flags: their joints are the regular lines behind the railing) and, through the lower curtain wall, on the pink haze outside.

Garden: planted cell by cell from a planting plan read off the painting (calibration/planting_plan.py -> data/planting.json): where the painting shows foliage up to a height above a cell, the cell carries plants that tall (ground cover, understory or shrubs); where it shows the pale floor it stays paved; cells seen only through glassware take their neighbours' class; cells the painting's camera cannot see are planted by design -- except the foot of the stair, the court along the north wall and the floor under the garden furniture.

Stair (dog-leg, solid stone treads): 14 treads (0.12308 m risers, 0.433 m goings) along x = -4.62..-3.12 rise from the garden at y = 0.32 to a landing at z = -1.354, then 11 treads turn west up to the gallery floor at x = -9.383; solved from the painted nosings (16 px rms).

Envelope: curtain walls on a 2 m module at x = -12.46 / 13.54 and y = -6 / 16, the roof's tie grid at z = 7.22 under a glass gable (volumes.Hall); the conservatory crowns a hilltop park whose north edge is its north wall: the frame's top row of image looks 6 degrees below the horizon, so the pink seen through the walls is the sunlit city haze in the valley below, not sky.  North of the wall a lower terrace of the hill lies 16 m below the gallery, reaching 33 m out -- just short of where its ground would rise above the sight line past the foot of the north wall, so the ground itself is never seen and the view beyond it falls into the haze; the trees on it, 30-45 m away, are the pale canopies seen through the north wall down to its foot (their tops placed on the painted canopy outline, their trunks and the terrace below every sight line through the wall), veiled by the haze between.  The faint tree further off stands on a lower terrace 84 m north (a crown 6.3 m wide, sized on its painted silhouette); that terrace, too, ends before it would rise above the sight line past the wall foot.

Garden specimens ("Painted ..."): each placed where its mass is in the painting -- the centre pixel of the mass back-projected through the solved camera at the height of its crown -- then shifted by whole 0.2 m steps where the rendered view then matches the painting better (calibration/layout_search.py); the random understory fills the beds between them.
Air: the sunlit air fills the conservatory 10 cm clear of the floor and roof.

Side table: the painting draws its top as an ellipse rounder (aspect 0.57) than a horizontal disc can project to at that place (every point on that view ray gives sin 26 deg = 0.44); the disc matches the painted width and centre, the objects on it their painted corners.

Sun: 55 deg high from azimuth 31 deg (to the right of and behind the atrium), so its shafts run down and to the left through the air as the painted ones do.  It shines through the city smog, which scatters the blue out of it: golden light (1, 0.85, 0.32) -- the painted sun patches on the pale pink floor are orange-yellow, not pink-white.

Shade trees: three umbrella trees in the unseen north-east of the garden (outside the painting frame) whose crowns stand between the sun and the paved court: their dappled shade is the green-and-pink mottling of the court floor seen through the balustrade, and the sun shafts come down between their leaves.

North wall: structurally glazed -- its panes meet on silicone joints, so only the transoms and the corner mullions are frames (the painting shows the pink haze through it undivided but for two horizontal bars).  Posts that the painting shows only below the gallery floor stop under it.

Daylight: the sky's light is 0.09 of the sun's power (sky.sun_ratio), the ratio that fits the painting best (a light fit at each of 0.03-0.26): the valley haze the light crosses dims the sky's share to that, and the painting's shadows are deep.  The fit scales both together.

Vines: climbing plants trained along the roof frame, 6.3-6.6 m above the gallery, above every sight line of the painting's camera: they are seen only in their dappled shade -- the leaf-shaped sun patches on the court, the treads and the gallery -- and in the shafts of sun between them.  The sun is the real sun, half a degree across, so the patches keep sharp edges from nine metres up.

City extent: the city ground and the haze reach 6 km out: the top row of the frame looks 6 degrees down, so its sight line meets the ground 1.2 km away -- inside the haze, where the ground has no edge to show.

Sky and haze as seen: a pale blue zenith and banks of pink-white cloud over a pink-white horizon (sky.clouds), seen by the camera at sky.seen_strength whatever share of the light the sky sheds; the valley haze thins out above the hilltop (materials.smog_top, smog_top_fade, smog_above) and the hilltop itself is clear air (smog_clear_min, smog_clear_max).  A sphere probe in every glass room (probes) lets its glass mirror the room, not the open sky.

Whole conservatory (volumes, collections Wings, Upper Floor, Conservatory Decor, Site, Wing Gardens): a fern house west, a palm house with a planted roof and a lantern east (the front door), a terrace house south under a planted roof terrace (the south door on the canal's axis), a glass stair tower to a belvedere at the south-east corner, a third-floor gallery round the atrium; all of it outside the painting's frame and away from its shadows, each step checked on the painting's probe.

Hall.notes: The gable over the painted hall, on its curtain walls (built as grids): ridge north-south at 14.7 m, the gable ends filled.

Fern House.notes: West wing: a gabled fern and tree-fern house whose ridge runs east-west, its east end open into the hall.

Palm House.notes: East wing and front door: a palm house glazed up to the third floor, its flat roof a planted ring round the lantern its palms grow up into.

Palm Lantern.notes: Clerestory and gable over the middle of the palm house, standing on its roof slab.

Terrace House.notes: South wing under the roof terrace: glass walls on three sides, its north side the hall; the south door ends the canal's axis.

Terrace.notes: The walkable glass roof of the south wing at the hall's third floor.

Stair Tower.notes: Glass stair tower at the hall's south-east corner, the conservatory's landmark: its flights climb past the hall's second and third floors to a belvedere under its own gable.

Canopy.notes: Flat glass canopy over the front door in the palm house's east wall.

Entrance Canopy.notes: Glass gable over the south door, where the canal's axis meets the conservatory.
